geometry.derivationNote: The treaty is already source-verified. The National Library of Finland catalogue now locates Kyösti Julku's specialist study devoted specifically to reconstructing the 1617 Stolbovo boundary, with mapped treatment of the line from the modern state border to Suolampi. The generic source-discovery state is therefore resolved, but this secondary reconstruction cannot by itself establish production geometry. Promotion remains blocked on acquisition/corroboration of the primary treaty or demarcation evidence, controlled georeferencing of the reconstructed sectors, and spatial validation.

The treaty text is already source-verified and an archival reproduction of Annex 1 to the German original is now located from the Politisches Archiv des Auswärtigen Amts; it shows the treaty demarcation line in blue. The generic source-discovery blocker is therefore resolved. Production geometry remains pending reproducible acquisition of the full relevant map extent, controlled georeferencing and spatial validation; the map must not be replaced by a later atlas trace.

Finlex's official 1969 frontier protocol identifies the 14 October 1920 Finland–RSFSR peace treaty as one of the instruments establishing the state boundary and states that the line on the ground is defined by signed boundary-description protocols, boundary maps, boundary-mark protocols and other demarcation records, including the 28 April 1938 package. The authoritative documentary/cartographic lineage is therefore located. Production geometry remains pending until those primary boundary materials are reproducibly acquired, rights-reviewed where needed, georeferenced and spatially validated.

Poland's Archiwum Akt Nowych preserves and publishes the original 18 March 1921 Treaty of Riga and identifies it as the decisive act establishing Poland's eastern boundary; its territorial Articles II–IV trace the Polish-Soviet frontier. The authoritative legal boundary description is therefore located. Production geometry remains pending controlled extraction of the line against authoritative period cartography/demarcation material and spatial validation.

Rosarchiv publishes the map accompanying the 12 March 1940 USSR-Finland peace treaty from the Archive of Foreign Policy of the Russian Federation (АВП РФ. Ф. 3а. Оп. 1. П. 44. Д. 279). The authoritative treaty cartography is therefore located. Production geometry remains pending until the source raster is captured with reproducibility metadata, commercial-use rights are reviewed, and controlled georeferencing/validation is completed.

effectiveDate.original: 30 января 1946 г. — обмен ратификационными грамотами в Праге
effectiveDate.note: UN Treaty Series No. 607 records entry into force on 30 January 1946, the date of exchange of instruments of ratification, under Article 2.

geometry.derivationNote: UNTS No. 607 fixes legal effect at the 30 January 1946 exchange of ratifications. The territorial polygon is reconstructed as the Trans-Carpathian-local component present in the verified 1945 USSR state and absent from the verified 1941 USSR state, with Uzhhorod/Mukachevo controls and neighboring exclusion controls. The 1974 frontier agreement independently confirms the 1945 treaty line and 1946 demarcation package.

territoryChanges.notes: Legacy id retains 1945 signature year, but replay now uses the treaty's verified 30 January 1946 entry-into-force date.

geometry.derivationNote: The 8 December agreement is a documentary state-transition milestone, not a cartographic subtraction from a continuing USSR polygon. It therefore does not define a new boundary line or area delta. Ratifications and later December instruments remain relevant to the exact constitutional termination/succession chronology, while the Russian Federation period begins independently in the coverage model.

territoryChanges.notes: Explicitly non-spatial for replay: do not derive post-Soviet state polygons from the Belovezha agreement itself.

geometry.derivationNote: Federal Constitutional Law No. 6-FKZ establishes the project legal-border scope/date; pinned public-domain Natural Earth 1:10m admin-1 polygons separately realize the Republic of Crimea and Sevastopol boundaries for deterministic replay. This geometry is canonical only for the project's russian-legal-border track and does not assert international recognition or de-facto control.

territoryChanges.notes: Geometry-verified for the Russian domestic legal-border track by combining the official legal definition with separately pinned Crimea and Sevastopol admin-1 polygons.
